text: Setting clear project goals is essential for success. A useful framework is to create SMART goals, which are Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, and Time-bound. For example, instead of saying “improve the website,” a SMART goal would be “increase website traffic by 20% within six months.” Once your main goals are set, break them into smaller milestones. These are checkpoints that help you track progress. Each milestone should have a clear deliverable, such as a finished report or a working prototype. Finally, ensure stakeholder alignment by discussing goals with everyone involved. This keeps the team focused and avoids misunderstandings later on.
